"I want to make a top down 3rd person RPG. The concept is a frustrated father raising 3 daughters. The girls are smart yet unruly and witting. The father has to accomplish household chores and attempt to get the 3 girls to help. He has to use his own wit and cleverness to get the girls to do chores. There is also a great pyrenees named Charlie who appears at times and adds to the chaos. he has the personality of a sterotypical great pyrenees. the girls names are Elaina, who is 12, elsie who is 9, and ellerie who is 5. The game starts in the morning with father in bed and the girls getting up at different times and waking up. he has to feed them, or convince them to work together to make breakfast for them selves. some of the tasks that need done are showers, doing laundry and dishes, etc. The day progresses to getting everyone in bed at night and everyone asleep. You win the game when everyone is asleep. Some things to take into consideration are everyones focus, and dad needs mental health breaks occassonally without losing his temper. If dad loses his temper too many times you lose the game. There should be on screen controls with buttons and arrows to move the dad around. The children characters on screen move on their own according to whatever each characters agenda is. the house should have 2 bedrooms. the girls all share one bedroom, the father has one bedroom. there is a bathroom with washer and dryer in it, and a kitchen and a living room. there are various distractions for the girls such as toys, tv, books and sometimes escaping outside. the girls also need breaks occasionally where they are allowed a distraction in order to stay on task.

---

- Build and verify a complete, playable top-down household RPG about Dad managing his daughters and Charlie through one chaotic Saturday.

## Requirements
- Include arrow-key and touch movement, autonomous children and dog behavior, meals, chores, chores, mood tracking, breathing breaks, and timed win/loss logic.
- Provide a visible on-screen interaction button for desktop and mobile, independent of keyboard availability.
- Keep the main `Interact` button enabled outside range and highlight it as ready only when Dad can perform the current task.

- Added both a persistent in-layout interaction button and a fixed mobile presentation.
- Use a ready-state green styling and pulse when Dad is within range of the active task.

- Built the complete house, character, schedule, task, meter, mood, and ending implementation in `index.html`.

## Objective
- Build and verify a complete, playable top-down household RPG about Dad managing his daughters and Charlie through one chaotic Saturday.

## Requirements
- Include arrow-key and touch movement, autonomous children and dog behavior, meals, chores, breathing breaks, mood tracking, and timed win/loss logic.
- Provide a persistent, visible interaction button for desktop and mobile that remains enabled outside range.
- Highlight the interaction button in green with a pulse only when Dad can perform the current task.
- Out-of-range interaction must provide closer-task feedback.
- Support full task progression, bedtime completion, temper loss, and restarting.

## Decisions
- Kept a persistent in-layout `Interact` button plus a fixed mobile presentation.
- Used a 55-game-coordinate-unit range for task readiness.
- Time parsing for bedtime was corrected to `20:00`.
- Tests set Dad directly onto task coordinates when verifying scripted progression.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the full house, schedule, character, chore, meter, mood, and ending implementation in `index.html`.
- Added keyboard/touch movement, autonomous behavior, breathing breaks, staggered wake times, and ACT controls.
- Fixed missing closing `</script>`, `</body>`, and `</html>` markup.
- Verified extracted JavaScript passes `node --check`.
- Verified desktop and mobile captures and confirmed no page JavaScript errors.
- Verified out-of-range `Interact` feedback.
- Verified breakfast readiness, green ready state, task completion, and chore advancement.
- Verified all 10 chores through scripted progression.
- Verified bedtime completion triggers the win state and shows the restart button.
- Verified stress reaching a third outburst triggers the loss state.
- Verified real touch movement changes Dad’s position on a mobile viewport.
- Verified the fixed mobile ACT button is visible and remains usable outside range.
- Verified the mobile ACT enters ready state when positioned at a task.

### Active
- Mobile ready-state ACT tapping needs direct final verification because Playwright `tap()` can see the pulsing button as unstable.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Complete a mobile-ready-state tap by replaying the `tap()` test in a stable viewport or pausing/validating the pulse animation.
2. Complete mobile end-state tapping and restart behavior through the live UI rather than scripted state injection.
3. Run a final desktop and mobile visual capture after gameplay state changes.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation, styles, UI, movement, tasks, and endings.
- `capture.sh`: Runs desktop/mobile browser captures.
- `start.sh`: Starts the local preview server.
- `/tmp/opencode/full-game-check.cjs`: Scripted verification for all chores, win, and loss.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-check.cjs`: Mobile touch, ACT, win, and restart verification script.
- `/tmp/opencode/test-household.cjs`: Desktop/mobile button and interaction checks.
- `/tmp/opencode/test-play.cjs`: Keyboard and desktop interaction verification.

## Important Context
- All implementation changes remain uncommitted.
- Game time begins at 7:00 AM; girls wake at 7:00, 7:22, and 7:44.
- Dad starts at `{x:170,y:135}`; breakfast is at `{x:552,y:350}`.
- Bedtime is at `20:00` and is the 10th/final chore.
- The ACT pulse can report the ready-state button as visually unstable under Playwright, so final mobile tapping needs careful test timing.
